name: Foreo Luna

card.summary: A handheld silicone facial-cleansing device that uses sonic pulsations to lift makeup and oil, aimed at leaving skin looking cleaner and smoother.
card.note: Silicone allergy is rare but reported by some users; independent clinical trials are scarce.

quick.overview:
The Foreo Luna is a battery-powered facial cleansing device with a soft silicone head instead of the nylon bristles of older cleansing brushes. Its pulsations are meant to loosen makeup, oil and dirt while feeling gentler on the skin, and the cleaner, less irritated skin is the appearance payoff people look for. Later models add a massage or firming mode.

It was Foreo's first product, from a Swedish company founded in 2013. Published support for its effects comes mainly from the manufacturer and consumer reviews, and independent clinical trials have not been published.
quick.how: Users apply a cleanser to the face and the silicone head, then move the device in small circles over the skin for a short time, usually as part of a morning or evening routine, rinsing afterwards and cleaning the device itself. Models differ in size, number of intensity settings and extra modes.
quick.risks: Silicone is generally described by users as gentle, though an allergy to silicone is possible in principle, and as with any cleansing tool, overuse or hard pressing can irritate skin. Users are advised to follow the maker's guidance.

lead: The Foreo Luna is a sonic facial cleansing device made by Foreo, a Stockholm-based company founded in 2013 by Filip Sedić. It was the company's first product, developed after its founder noticed skin irritation from conventional facial brushes, and it replaces nylon bristles with silicone [1].

The pitch for looks is cleaner, clearer-looking skin: pulsations help lift makeup and oil, and the silicone is intended to be gentler than bristles. Foreo later added devices such as the ISSA toothbrush (2014), IRIS eye massager (2016), ESPADA blue-LED acne device (2017), UFO sheet-mask device (2018) and BEAR microcurrent device (2020) [1].
Support for specific results comes mostly from the manufacturer and consumer reviews; no independent clinical trial of the Luna is known.

chain: Silicone head pulses against cleanser on the face
Makeup, oil and dirt are loosened and rinsed away
Skin looks cleaner and feels smoother
angle.text: People use it in place of hands or a cloth when washing their face, hoping for cleaner pores and a smoother look. It also doubles as a short facial massage.

infobox: Per Wikipedia, Foreo's ESPADA and BEAR devices have FDA clearance

paras: The device is a handheld unit with a silicone head covered in short soft projections that pulse at sonic frequencies, replacing the nylon bristles of conventional brushes [1]. Users describe the feel as closer to a gentle facial massage than to scrubbing, and later models add firming or massage settings.

Foreo was established in Stockholm in 2013 and entered the US market in 2014 [1]. Forbes has reported more than 36 million Foreo products sold by 2021, according to Wikipedia [1]. The Luna line has since expanded through multiple generations, including mini versions and a Luna 4.

Consumer reviews of the Luna range are mixed in the way reviews of cleansing tools usually are: many praise softness and gentleness, while others say they cannot tell the result from washing with a cloth and a cleanser. Many published reviews come from the brand or retailers rather than independent testers.

timeline.event: Foreo founded in Stockholm by Filip Sedić; Luna is its first product [1].
Foreo enters the US market and launches the ISSA toothbrush [1].
Forbes reports over 36 million products sold [1].
